15.0.s.en: (1) The resurrection of Christ and His appearances

15.0.0.en: It appears that some people in the Church of Corinth had denied the resurrection, like the Sadducee Jews or the Greek philosophers.

15.0.1.en: “I declare unto you”: I am amazed at your unbelief, as though you had never before heard in my preaching to you of the essential doctrines, of which the most important is the teaching of the resurrection. And if you have believed in it and live in it, it saves you as long as you hold fast to it, unless your faith is theoretical and you do not apply it in your life.

15.1.0.en: I inform you, brethren, that the most important thing in the good news that I and you have believed is the death of Christ for our sins to redeem us, and that He was buried in the presence of His disciples and then rose on the third day, as the prophecies declared in the Old Testament.

15.2.0.en: In verses 5 to 8 St. Paul enumerates some of the appearances of Christ after His resurrection, in the order in which they occurred. He appeared to Peter, then to the twelve (“the twelve” became a name for the company of the disciples, according to the original number applied to them, regardless of their number in a given circumstance; for on the day of this appearance they were only ten, because Judas had perished and Thomas was not with them.)

15.3.0.en: Then He appeared to five hundred brethren; although the Gospels do not give a clear indication of this appearance, it was most probably the day He appeared to the disciples in Galilee, as He had said to them before His death, “But after I am risen again, I will go before you into Galilee” (Mt 26:32), and as He said to the two women on the morning of His resurrection, “Go tell my brethren that they go into Galilee, and there shall they see me” (Mt 28:10). Most of these witnesses were still alive about thirty years after the appearance of Christianity, so that anyone who doubts could ask them, and some of them had fallen asleep. The Church uses the expression “falling asleep” to indicate that the bodies of Christians are resting in their graves, awaiting their resurrection on the last day.

15.4.0.en: After that He appeared to James, then to all the Apostles, which is the appearance mentioned in (Jn 20:26) or in (Acts 1:4).

15.5.0.en: Seven or eight years after the Ascension of Christ, He appeared to Paul, who was then on his way to Damascus (Acts 9:3, 4). St. Paul likened himself to one born out of due time, that is, an immature child born before its time, because of his sense of unworthiness of the grace that Christ showed him.

15.5.1.en: God appears in your life in many forms, whether in His generous gifts or through afflictions; may you hold fast to Him and not turn aside from Him as your one aim in all your steps.

15.6.0.en: For I am the least of the Apostles in the apostolic ministry, and am not worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the Church of God. The Apostle said this out of his great humility and his deep regret over what he did before his faith. This humility did not prevent him from declaring his apostolic authority and the obedience due to him, so that people would obey his teaching for the glory of Christ and for the establishing of the truths he proclaimed, as he said in (2 Cor 11:5, 12:11).

15.7.0.en: “I am what I am”: my strength is not from myself but from God.

15.7.1.en: This grace that was given to him was not in vain but gave him strength for preaching; he founded more churches than the rest of the Apostles and wrote more books of the Holy Bible than all of them; yet he does not attribute his success in the ministry to himself, but all of this was by the grace of God working in him.

15.8.0.en: Whether it was I or the other Apostles, we preach the resurrection of Christ from the dead, which is the fundamental subject on which our preaching is built, and by your accepting the faith you have also believed in the resurrection.

15.8.1.en: The grace of God that worked in St. Paul is ready to work in you if you believe and hold fast to it with earnestness in prayers, and feel your weakness more than all, so that the glory may be to God, and give all your effort to show your seriousness and your concern for what you ask of God.

15.9.s.en: (2) The result of not believing in the resurrection

15.9.0.en: If we have proved the truth of Christ’s resurrection by conclusive proofs in our preaching, how do some of you say that there is no resurrection of the dead, that is, that man perishes at his death and there is no other life after death?

15.10.0.en: Every objection to the general resurrection is an objection to the resurrection of Christ Himself. For if there is no resurrection of the dead, this means that Christ has not risen, whereas the resurrection of Christ is certain to all because He took our body and rose in it.

15.11.0.en: If Christ has not truly risen, then our preaching, we the Apostles, is not true. For we have preached that Christ rose, and that He is now alive and able to save whoever believes in Him, and if Christ has not risen all that becomes in vain, because a dead man cannot save the living. The foundation of your faith in Christ is your faith in His resurrection and that He is now seated at the right hand of the Father in heaven. If He has not risen, the foundation of your faith is falsehood and illusion and of no avail.

15.12.0.en: Thus we become liars and false pretenders, because we give false witness concerning God in saying that God raised Christ, and this could not have happened if your belief that the dead do not rise were true.

15.13.0.en: For if the dead do not rise, this means in consequence that Christ has not risen, since He took a body like our body.

15.14.0.en: Christ died on our behalf to pay the price of sin. If Christ has not risen, it means that the debt of sin has not yet been paid, because the wages of sin is death. But since He has risen, He has satisfied divine justice.

15.15.0.en: As a result of the preceding verse, those who have died having faith and hope in Christ have perished, if there is no resurrection.

15.15.1.en: Remember every morning, with the prayer of Prime in the Agpeya, the resurrection of Christ, that it may give you strength for a new beginning, so that you put away the sins of the past and walk circumspectly, and enjoy a fellowship with Christ that fills your heart with joy however much sorrows surround you, and so gain the ability to break through difficulties and to succeed by His grace.

15.16.s.en: (3) We have a hope in the resurrection

15.16.0.en: If our hope, through our faith in Christ, is directed only to this earthly life, how wretched we are. For Christ did not give His followers a promise of any glory in this world; rather He made clear that whoever follows Him will pass through tribulation and pain and be exposed to many persecutions, but He promised us a hope of an eternal inheritance in His Kingdom after the resurrection.

15.17.0.en: But Christ has truly risen from the dead, and this resurrection of His is the pledge of the resurrection of those who have fallen asleep in the hope of eternal glory.

15.17.1.en: “The firstfruits of them that slept”: although He is not the first to rise from the dead, since there were those whom Elijah and Elisha raised, and those He Himself raised, such as Lazarus, the daughter of Jairus and the son of the widow of Nain, yet He was distinguished from them in that He raised Himself, and likewise did not die a second time; besides this, He rose to raise us up in Himself, for He died, though without sin, on our behalf to redeem us.

15.18.0.en: If death entered the human race through the first Adam, who transgressed God’s commandment, so also through the second Adam, who is Christ, the resurrection from the dead is accomplished. Every son of Adam inherits death from him, and every son of Christ inherits eternal life from Him.

15.19.0.en: For as Adam bequeathed death to his descendants, so also by the believers’ union with Christ they shall live.

15.19.1.en: This makes clear the first condition of salvation, which is faith in Christ, His death and His resurrection.

15.20.0.en: “In his own order”: in the original Greek it came with the meaning of in succession or in turn, that is, each one in his turn. Christ rose first as the firstfruits, and after Him the believers will rise at the Second Coming to live the eternal glory. The turn of mankind comes on the Day of Judgment, and they are glorified with Christ.

15.20.1.en: The phrase “every man in his own order” also indicates that the reward after the resurrection is according to the labor of each one; there are degrees in the eternal glory, to urge us to exert more effort here for God so that we may have the eternal reward.

15.20.2.en: The hope of eternity fills your heart with joy at what God has prepared for you, so you endure the sufferings of the temporary life, for however hard or long they are, they will end. On the other hand, you feel a drive for spiritual striving in worship and service to obtain the great reward in heaven.

15.20.3.en: May you think five minutes every day about the eternity that awaits you.

15.21.0.en: After the Second Coming of Christ and the general resurrection will come the end of the present world and the end of the dispensation of salvation. The delivering up of the kingdom is easy to understand if we compare Christ’s kingdom over the present world with His eternal Kingdom, when there will be no rule or authority for the devil; accordingly, the delivering up of the kingdom to God the Father means that Christ has completed what was required of Him, which is redemption, and delivered it to the Father who sent Him to accomplish this mission. The delivering up of the kingdom to the Father does not mean that the Son does not reign, because the Father and the Son are one in essence.

15.22.0.en: For Christ, to Him be the glory, must reign with absolute dominion over all, which will be accomplished in eternity after the Second Coming, when all the demons and the wicked will be subjected under the feet of Christ and cast into eternal torment.

15.23.0.en: Death is an enemy because it entered the world through sin and was a punishment for it. To do away with death, the causes that led to it must be abolished. This is what was accomplished by redemption: Christ abolished death by the resurrection after He abolished all the causes that led to death, which are due to the envy of the devil. That is, He defeated the devil and his forces with a final defeat, and thereby abolished the death that the devil caused.

15.24.0.en: The Father put all things under the feet of Christ, to Him be the glory, but it is clear that God the Father is not included among those subjected to Christ, because it is He who subjected all things to the Son, so He is not included among the things that are subjected to the Son. This is a preparation for the following verse.

15.25.1.en: “In all”: God will be in all the believers, united with them and reigning over their hearts forever.

15.25.2.en: What is meant by the Son’s subjection to His Father is the complete subjection of humanity, in the Son, to the Father. For the Son put on the body of man and died for mankind to remove all causes of disobedience and sin, and to lead all, in the body of His humanity, to obedience to His Father; so the Son presents to the Father a new, complete world, so that the one God in three hypostases may be reigning over all.

15.25.3.en: That is, the Son will be subject to the Father not hypostatically but in respect of His being man; for the hypostases are not subject to one another, but their works are all subject to one another in completeness, harmony and a preconceived divine dispensation). See Rev 11:15, Lk 1:33, Dan 7:14) concerning the eternity of Christ’s kingdom.

15.25.4.en: So we have one God in three hypostases. And thanks be to God through Christ Jesus our Lord, who obeyed and was content to be subject to death in order to complete our salvation, and who is one with His good Father and the Holy Spirit, forever and ever.

15.25.5.en: Your subjection to God and obedience to His commandments rescue you from the bondage of sin and the humiliation Satan inflicts on you, because when you submit to your tender God, He raises you by His love to the degree of sonship, gives you the enjoyment of His company, and even glorifies you with Him in heaven.

15.25.6.en: So ask yourself every day, when you examine yourself, to what extent have you submitted to God’s commandments?

15.26.0.en: Many of the pagans used to witness the death of the martyrs and would believe and be baptized. Why would they do this if the dead do not rise?

15.26.1.en: Is not this behavior of theirs, in accepting death in imitation of the martyrs, a witness to the truth of the resurrection of the dead? There is another view in the interpretation of this verse, which is the appearance of a heresy in the first century that said that if a catechumen who was learning the faith died before being baptized, another could be baptized in his place; so Paul says to those who follow this heresy, why are they baptized for the catechumens who have died if the dead do not rise? Of course Paul does not approve of this heresy, but he uses their error to prove the resurrection of the dead.

15.26.2.en: There is a third view, which is that “the dead” refers to the sufferings and persecutions undergone by those who come to the faith: why would they accept Baptism and the endurance of death every day if there is no other life after this present life that is full of suffering?!

15.27.0.en: Why do we the Apostles expose ourselves to dangers for the sake of preaching the Gospel, if we have no hope in the resurrection and in eternal life?!

15.28.0.en: “By your rejoicing which I have”: my boasting is in your faith.

15.28.1.en: “In Christ Jesus”: by the grace and help of Christ.

15.28.2.en: “I die daily”: I am exposed to death during preaching and ministry.

15.28.3.en: Paul declares his joy and boasting in the faith of the Corinthians, and this drives him to greater service and exposure to suffering and death so that their faith may grow and increase, and the grace of Christ supports him in this.

15.29.0.en: If I were like a man, with merely human motives, concerned only with this life and not believing in the resurrection and eternal life, what would be the benefit of all my facing of the many wars and the great resistance from the opponents of the preaching at Ephesus?

15.29.1.en: If there is no resurrection after death, then let our motto be the motto of those who do not believe in eternal life, which is: let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die. That is, not believing in the resurrection would make the endurance of suffering in the ministry useless and would drive us to indulge in material lusts.

15.30.0.en: Do not submit to the evil ideas of the world that encourage bad desires. The Apostle advises them to cut off their relations with their former pagan companions, lest by associating with them their good morals be corrupted.

15.31.0.en: He guides them to be watchful in order to do all that is good and not expose themselves to committing sins, because there were people living in their midst who deny the resurrection and are ignorant of God’s power, justice and goodness. He alerts them by this in order to stir their shame at such mistaken beliefs.

15.31.1.en: The risen Christ conquered death to urge us to be strong and conquer every sin, and also not to yield to any obstacles that hinder us from doing good. So when you meet any problem, remember your risen Christ and ask His help and go forward without fear, and God will deliver you from all afflictions.

15.32.0.en: St. Paul supposed that an objector asks these two questions, showing the impossibility of the bodies rising after their corruption and dissolution, and that even if these bodies rose they would not be suited to the immortal spiritual state in heaven.

15.33.0.en: We conclude from the Apostle’s answer that most of the objection is built on an illusion, which is that the resurrection body is the very same as the present body with its instincts and organs. So he rebukes them, showing them their ignorance in rejecting a doctrine that God has shown to mankind in the world of plants. The seed cannot sprout stems, leaves and flowers unless it is placed in the earth and buried to die, so that the change from the form of the seed to the form of the plant may occur, although the seed and the plant have the same essence.

15.34.0.en: The seed changes completely into the plant that comes out of it. You sow a grain of wheat and it sprouts a plant entirely different from the grain in form, but not different from it in essence; every seed yields fruit after its kind, as God said in the Book of Genesis (Gen 1:12).

15.35.0.en: To every seed God gives, as He willed, its own plant body, which distinguishes it from the other plants; and although all plant bodies share the same constituents, they are distinguished from one another in the particular form of each body.

15.36.0.en: So also with the bodies of animals: although each is flesh and blood, they differ greatly from one another. The body of man is not the body of beasts, nor the body of fish, nor the body of birds. That is, God made the bodies of animals differ to suit the conditions in which the animal lives, whether on the earth, in the water or in the air. This shows us that our bodies in heaven will differ in form from our earthly bodies to suit our heavenly state, although they are the same essence as the earthly body, but changed so that it becomes spiritual and lives forever.

15.37.0.en: The Apostle mentions the distinction between the heavenly bodies (the sun, the moon, the stars and the other planets) and the earthly bodies (plants and animals) as evidence of the distinction between man’s body in this present life and his body in the resurrection. The heavenly bodies differ from the earthly bodies in appearance and in the nature of their making, and likewise man’s material body on earth will differ from his spiritual body in heaven, which will be in great glory.

15.38.0.en: The brightness of the sun differs from the brightness of the moon. And the stars differ among themselves in the power of their light and brilliance and in other properties of each. The difference is not only between beings different in their nature but also between those of the same nature. Although the stars have one general nature, they differ among themselves.

15.38.1.en: So it is with the risen bodies: the righteous will differ in glory, and likewise the wicked among themselves in the degrees of eternal torment.

15.39.0.en: Thus the resurrection body excels our present body. Man’s body in earthly life is exposed to factors of dissolution and corruption when it is buried, but in the resurrection it becomes incorruptible, not subject to weakness, death and dissolution.

15.40.0.en: When the body of the mortal is laid in the grave, everything it had of beauty, strength and majesty leaves it, but in the resurrection it is raised in the image of Christ, and is in the utmost beauty and perfection of strength, as the Apostle says in (Phil 3:21), “Who will change the form of our lowly body that it may be conformed to the body of His glory.” Nothing is weaker than the corpse of the dead, for it is unable to do anything or defend itself, but at the resurrection the mortal is raised in a power suited to the new immortal life, and is not subject to any weakness or weariness.

15.41.0.en: Man has a body suited to his nature, and on earth he shares it with all other living beings, and he has an animal soul that contains the instincts (what is meant by the soul here is the vitality in the body that moves all its organs and ends at his death.) But in the resurrection he will have a spiritual body led by the spirit, suited to his glorified nature, and in heaven he shares it with the pure angels.

15.41.1.en: If you believe in the existence of the first man, you must believe in the existence of the second. When the body is raised from the dead it is changed into the spiritual body.

15.41.2.en: The natural body is led by the animal soul that results from the union of the spirit with the body, whereas the spiritual body is led by the spirit, because its body is without instincts. For the animal soul does not share with the body and the spirit in the resurrection, but dissolves as soon as a person dies and does not rise.

15.42.0.en: The Lord God formed Adam of the dust of the ground (Gen 2:7), and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, that is, the spirit, and Adam became a living soul from the union of the body with the spirit.

15.42.1.en: And the last Adam, who is Christ, to Him be the glory, after His resurrection came to have a spiritual body and was called a quickening spirit, because He has the power to give life to others, and the Spirit leads Him after the resurrection without there being an animal soul; He is spirit and a spiritual body, and there is no animal soul that moves the material body with all its instincts.

15.43.0.en: The order mentioned in this verse agrees with what we see in all the works of God. We sow the seed in the earth, and the fruit or the tree comes first below the ground and then above it; the imperfect precedes the perfect, our bodily birth precedes our spiritual birth, and earthly life precedes the heavenly.

15.44.0.en: The first man, who is Adam, was earthy because his body was created from the earth and was suited to dwelling in it.

15.44.1.en: The second man: He is the incarnate Christ, and He is from heaven in respect of His divinity, as the Scripture says, “he that came down from heaven, even the Son of man which is in heaven” (Jn 3:13). St. Paul’s aim is to say that Adam is from the earth and it is evident that we are like him here; and Christ is from heaven and we shall be like Him there, that is, with spiritual bodies led by the spirit without animal instincts.

15.45.0.en: As Adam’s body was of the dust of the earth and is marked by weakness and liability to decay and corruption, so also are the descendants of Adam, because our bodies are of dust like his. And as Christ was the one who came down from heaven, so the believers in Him, the baptized, who have become His sons, at the resurrection will be in the image of the body of His glory in heaven.

15.46.0.en: As we inherited from Adam his weak nature, liable to sickness, pain and death, so by the resurrection our bodies will become like the glorified body of Christ.

15.46.1.en: It is fitting for us to benefit from the possibilities of our new life by Baptism, which qualifies us for a glorified, heavenly life after the resurrection and gives us the ability to triumph over the evil enemy in the present world, so that we walk in purity and love toward all, and use the world and are not enslaved to it.

15.47.0.en: The natural man is composed of the body (flesh and blood), the soul and the spirit. The body in its present state is liable to decay and corruption, and therefore cannot be immortal in heaven; the corruptible body cannot inherit the incorruptible Kingdom of Heaven.

15.48.0.en: I reveal to you a truth that was unknown but which the Spirit of God has revealed to us, which is that the people who are alive at the Second Coming of Christ will not die, but all of us, whether we are among these or among those who have fallen asleep, will have our bodies changed and take on new characteristics suited to the life of immortality.

15.49.0.en: The time of the shout of the angels and the last trumpet at the Second Coming is the moment of the change, in which the bodies of the living will be changed into incorruptible bodies, and in which also the dead will rise with incorruptible bodies.

15.50.0.en: This change must take place, because this corruptible body must be transformed into incorruption, and the mortal must become immortal, with the characteristics of immortality and eternity.

15.51.0.en: When our bodies have risen possessing the characteristics of immortality and eternal life, and the body has been transformed from a corruptible body into one not subject to corruption, death will no longer have dominion over us, and there will be fulfilled what Isaiah foretold, “He will swallow up death forever” (Isa 25:8), and as Hosea foretold, “O death, where are thy plagues? O grave, where is thy sting?” (Hos 13:14).

15.52.0.en: A rhetorical question that the Apostle takes from the prophet Hosea, by which he wanted to say that the dominion of death and Hades has ended forever by the resurrection of Christ. He likened death to a poisonous stinger like the scorpion, whose sting is deadly like a plague. And he addressed the grave, or the dwelling of the dead, as though it were a cruel jailer who held sway over mankind through the ages but was finally broken and released its captives forever.

15.53.0.en: Sin is the weapon by which death gained dominion over us, for whoever has not sinned does not fear death. The Law exposes sin and helps a person to recognize it and to feel its deadly authority, as though it had been given power to put to death the person who commits it.

15.54.0.en: Finally the Apostle gives thanks to God, who gave us the victory and provided the means of obtaining it by the resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ from the dead.

15.55.0.en: On the basis of the preceding proofs of the truth of the resurrection, I ask you, beloved, not to give heed to the false teachers who wanted to lead you to deny that fundamental doctrine of the Christian faith, and be steadfast in the faith of the Gospel, and abound in works whose aim is the glorifying of the Lord at all times; for the Lord will not forget what the believer has done or endured in his service, and will recompense him with a glorious resurrection, immortal life and a heavenly reward.

15.55.1.en: If eternal glories await us, let this drive us to every good work, and let us seize the opportunity of life to do good and show mercy to everyone, so that we may have greater glory in heaven.

15.55.2.en: The First Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians. The final instructions and greeting
